chunk.text: For a boosting step, approximate each loss by a second-order Taylor expansion around the current prediction. Aggregate first derivatives G and second derivatives H in each leaf. With an L2 penalty lambda on leaf weights, the stationary weight is -G/(H+lambda). A candidate split is evaluated by the improvement from separate left and right leaf scores, subtracting the additional leaf penalty. This derivation explains why Hessian statistics influence split selection.

  91  |      3     |   2  |      2

chunk.text: A 95 percent confidence procedure produces intervals that cover the fixed population parameter in 95 percent of repeated samples under its assumptions. The particular interval calculated from one sample either covers the parameter or does not. A wider interval reflects less precision, not necessarily a larger effect. Changing the sample design or violating independence can invalidate the advertised coverage.
